title: Closing the Efficiency Gap: Cost-to-Income to 48% by 2028
brief:
Board presentation in a consulting style for Meridian Gulf Bank, a mid-size retail bank in the UAE. Topic: how we bring our cost-to-income ratio down from 58% to 48% by 2028. Audience: the board of directors and the CFO. Facts to use: our cost-to-income ratio is 58% today; the peer median is 49% and the best-in-class regional bank is at 41%. Three levers: branch network consolidation (-4.0 points), digital migration of service transactions (-3.5 points), procurement and vendor consolidation (-2.5 points). Phasing: 2026 design and quick wins (58% to 55%), 2027 scale (55% to 51%), 2028 run-rate (51% to 48%). One-off investment AED 420 million over three years; run-rate savings AED 310 million a year from 2028. Generate EXACTLY 5 slides.

PREFLIGHT ANSWERS:
- Tone: formal, analytical, board-ready
- Visual style: clean consulting style, light background, charts over imagery
- Brand colour: deep teal

slides.title: Meridian Gulf Bank: Bringing Cost-to-Income from 58% to 48% by 2028
slides.subtitle: Board of Directors | Efficiency programme recommendation
slides.visual: Clean light cover with a deep teal band and a single thin line sweeping down from 58 to 48 across the page, the two numbers set large at either end, with the bank's name in small caps above.
slides.speaker_note: Today we ask the board to endorse a three-year programme that closes our efficiency gap to peers and sets us up to lead the region.

slides.title: At 58%, we spend 9 points more than the peer median and 17 more than the best regional bank
slides.subtitle: Cost-to-income ratio, retail banks in the region
key_points: Closing to 48% puts us at peer level by 2028
slides.visual: A horizontal bar exhibit of three bars on a light background: Meridian at 58% in deep teal, peer median at 49% and best-in-class at 41% in muted grey, with bracketed callouts marking the 9-point and 17-point gaps and a dashed target line at 48%.
slides.speaker_note: We are not an outlier by accident. Each point of ratio is real money, and the gap to the median is the first thing to close. Our target of 48% takes us just inside the peer median.

slides.title: Three levers deliver the 10-point reduction, led by branch consolidation at 4.0 points
slides.subtitle: Cost-to-income reduction by lever, percentage points
key_points: Digital migration of service transactions: minus 3.5 points
Procurement and vendor consolidation: minus 2.5 points
slides.visual: A waterfall exhibit stepping down from 58% through three teal-toned bars of 4.0, 3.5 and 2.5 points to a final 48% bar, each step labelled with its lever name and value, the total drop bracketed on the right.
slides.speaker_note: The programme rests on three levers, each with a clear owner. Branch consolidation is the largest, digital migration is the most scalable, and procurement is the fastest to start.

slides.title: We get there in three phases: 55% in 2026, 51% in 2027, 48% in 2028
slides.subtitle: Programme phasing and ratio milestones
key_points: Each phase has a board checkpoint before the next begins
slides.visual: Three columns on a horizontal timeline, one per year, each topped by a large ratio figure in teal (55%, 51%, 48%) and a short list beneath of what happens that year, linked by a descending line that connects the milestones.
slides.speaker_note: The path is front-loaded with quick wins to build credibility, then scales through 2027 and reaches run-rate in 2028. The board sees progress against each milestone annually.

slides.title: AED 420 million invested over three years returns AED 310 million a year from 2028
slides.subtitle: Decision requested from the board
key_points: One-off investment: AED 420 million across 2026 to 2028
Run-rate savings: AED 310 million every year from 2028
Payback in roughly 16 months of run-rate savings
Request: approve the programme and the 2026 phase budget
slides.visual: Two large teal figures side by side, AED 420m one-off investment on the left and AED 310m annual run-rate savings on the right, joined by a bold arrow, with a slim decision box along the bottom stating the approval requested.
slides.speaker_note: The investment is one-off and the savings recur every year. We ask the board to approve the programme today so that design and quick wins can start in 2026.
